Purpose and exclusions

TargetActor Object(AActor), HomeLocation Vector, HasTarget Bool, Leashing Bool, AttackRange Float cm

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create the matching Editor asset after native row/key types are ready. Populate the listed keys/rows exactly; a renamed key needs consumer updates.
  2. Assign to its AI controller or definition; run the linked fixture and reject missing rows/keys.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in NavMesh AI, perception, threat, leash and evade. Rule owner: ARPGEnemyAIController. This asset’s role is TargetActor Object(AActor), HomeLocation Vector, HasTarget Bool, Leashing Bool, AttackRange Float cm

  1. Spawn controller possesses the enemy Character and initializes definition, ASC and Blackboard before running the Behavior Tree.
  2. Perception updates candidate targets; a target selector combines disposition/threat/leash rules and writes one Blackboard TargetActor.
  3. Behavior Tree moves with navigation, chooses attack when range/LOS/cooldown permit, and calls the same authoritative ability stack as player attacks.
  4. Damage/healing contribution emits verified threat; threat does not come from client UI selection or proximity alone.
  5. If target is unreachable/outside leash or combat stalls, enter Evade: cancel attacks/projectiles owned by this reset, clear threat/credit according to policy and navigate home.
  6. After reaching a valid home floor, restore health under reset policy and resume patrol. Defeated state instead hands off to the unique defeat/loot record; it cannot evade back to life after rewards committed.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / Encounter_WestRoad / LeashBoundary / Bridge. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Target behind unreachable ledge -> pursue/reposition or evade; no platformer X-axis chase heuristic.
Player kites beyond leash -> encounter resets safely and no reward is emitted.
Target disconnects -> choose remaining valid threat or reset; no null-target attack.
Two clients damage one enemy -> server threat/credit are consistent; client order does not determine final ledger identity.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
